name: scan0007-text-0182
text: Introductory Note.

name: scan0007-text-0183
text: The Liberty engine is of the ungeared twelve-

name: scan0007-text-0184
text: cylinder Vee type, with cylinders set at 45°. The bore

name: scan0007-text-0185
text: is 5 in. (127 mm.), and the stroke 7 in. (177.8 mm.). The

name: scan0007-text-0186
text: “dry” weight is 820 lbs. The engine is constructed in two

name: scan0007-text-0187
text: models, the army type having a higher compression

name: scan0007-text-0188
text: ratio (5.3 : 1) than the naval type (4.78 : 1); the maximum

name: scan0007-text-0189
text: r.p.m. of both types are 1750, at which speed 425

name: scan0007-text-0190
text: b.h.p. is developed by the army type, its normal b.h.p.

name: scan0007-text-0191
text: being 405 at 1650 r.p.m. The naval type is not used in

name: scan0007-text-0192
text: the British Service at present; it gives 396 h.p. at 1,650

name: scan0007-text-0193
text: r.p.m.

name: scan0007-text-0194
text: The water-cooled cylinders are constructed from

name: scan0007-text-0195
text: steel tube with welded jackets: there are two valves per

name: scan0007-text-0196
text: cylinder.

name: scan0007-text-0197
text: The pistons, cylinders, and gudgeon pins are lubri-

name: scan0007-text-0198
text: cated by splash. Oil is pressure-fed to the rest of the

name: scan0007-text-0199
text: engine, including the camshafts. The sump is scavenged

name: scan0007-text-0200
text: by a three-pinion pump combined in a unit with the pres-

name: scan0007-text-0201
text: sure pump, and located in the rear oil well.

name: scan0007-text-0202
text: Ignition is by the Delco system. A twelve-point

name: scan0007-text-0203
text: distributor, embodying two contact breakers in parallel,

name: scan0007-text-0204
text: is mounted on the rear end of each camshaft, and supplied

name: scan0007-text-0205
text: with current for starting and at low engine speeds by

name: scan0007-text-0206
text: an accumulator. When the engine attains 650 r.p.m.,

name: scan0007-text-0207
text: the current is furnished by a dynamo generator,

name: scan0007-text-0208
text: mounted between the inclined camshaft drives at the

name: scan0007-text-0209
text: rear of the engine. This generator further charges the

name: scan0007-text-0210
text: accumulator. An auxiliary circuit breaker on each dis-

name: scan0007-text-0211
text: tributor head prevents the engine from firing in a reverse

name: scan0007-text-0212
text: direction.

name: scan0007-text-0213
text: Two duplex Zenith carburettors (type 52 D.F.) of

name: scan0007-text-0214
text: American manufacture are fitted on the engines now being

name: scan0007-text-0215
text: delivered, but later engines will be equipped with two

name: scan0007-text-0216
text: Claudel-Hobson carburettors, type H.C. 7.

name: scan0007-text-0217
text: An electric starter is to be fitted, for which a

name: scan0007-text-0218
text: special handbook will be published in due course.

name: scan0013-text-0676
text: General Description.

name: scan0013-text-0677
text: In the following descriptions, the propeller end of

name: scan0013-text-0678
text: the engine is termed the “front”; the words “right”

name: scan0013-text-0679
text: and “left” are used on the supposition that the engine

name: scan0013-text-0680
text: is viewed from the rear or distribution gear end.

name: scan0014-text-0685
text: CYLINDERS.

name: scan0014-text-0686
text: Each cylinder is formed from a steel tube, the head,

name: scan0014-text-0687
text: barrel, flange and spigot being all in one piece. One

name: scan0014-text-0688
text: end of the tube is closed down to form the cylinder head,

name: scan0014-text-0689
text: and seatings for the two valves are machined in it.

name: scan0014-text-0690
text: The holding-down flange is “jumped up” after local

name: scan0014-text-0691
text: heating, leaving a spigot 2

name: scan0014-text-0695
text: in. deep. The water jacket

name: scan0014-text-0696
text: is made of two sheet steel pressings, welded together:

name: scan0014-text-0697
text: the line of the main vertical joint is at right angles to

name: scan0014-text-0698
text: the crankshaft axis. There are further welded joints at

name: scan0014-text-0699
text: the two valve pockets, sparking plug bosses, upper and

name: scan0014-text-0700
text: lower water connections, camcase studs, and round the

name: scan0014-text-0701
text: base of the jacket.

name: scan0014-text-0702
text: The cylinders are interchangeable, though the long

name: scan0014-text-0703
text: and short studs supporting the camcase must be inter-

name: scan0014-text-0704
text: changed before a right-hand cylinder can be mounted in

name: scan0014-text-0705
text: the left-hand block and vice versâ. (See Fig. 2.)

name: scan0014-text-0706
text: The holding-down flanges are drilled for ten studs

name: scan0014-text-0707
text: apiece. Flats are cut through the two stud holes on

name: scan0014-text-0708
text: the fore and aft sides of each flange, so that the two studs

name: scan0014-text-0709
text: between a pair of cylinders secure both flanges. The

name: scan0014-text-0710
text: holding-down nuts are made with circular bases of

name: scan0014-text-0711
text: greater diameter than their hexagons.

name: scan0014-text-0712
text: Fig. 4.

name: scan0014-text-0713
text: Cylinder Head (plan view).

name: scan0015-text-0715
text: PISTONS.

name: scan0015-text-0716
text: Fig. 4 affords a plan view of a cylinder head, illus-

name: scan0015-text-0717
text: trating the large water space round each valve pocket

name: scan0015-text-0718
text: and the positions of the sparking plug bosses, camcase

name: scan0015-text-0719
text: studs, and water exit pipe: the latter is jointed by a

name: scan0015-text-0720
text: rubber connection to a short pipe projecting from the

name: scan0015-text-0721
text: water jacket of one of the four induction manifolds.

name: scan0015-text-0722
text: The circumference of each cylinder jacket increases

name: scan0015-text-0723
text: gradually towards the top of the piston stroke. The

name: scan0015-text-0724
text: water entry connections are short pipes, curving down-

name: scan0015-text-0725
text: wards from the base of each jacket on the outside of

name: scan0015-text-0726
text: the block.

name: scan0015-text-0727
text: The high compression pistons (Fig. 7) are of cast

name: scan0015-text-0728
text: aluminium alloy with externally domed tops, flattened

name: scan0015-text-0729
text: at the centre over a circle 2

name: scan0015-text-0733
text: in. in diameter. (The low

name: scan0015-text-0734
text: compression pistons have flat tops). There are no

name: scan0015-text-0735
text: internal ribs, but the crown is

name: scan0015-text-0739
text: in. thick, and the upper

name: scan0015-text-0740
text: part of the wall tapers down towards the gudgeon pin

name: scan0015-text-0741
text: bosses. There are three compression rings above the

name: scan0015-text-0742
text: Fig. 5.

name: scan0015-text-0743
text: Side View of a Cylinder.

name: scan0016-text-0745
text: gudgeon pin: each ring has a diagonal gap, and a

name: scan0016-text-0746
text: shallow circumferential oil groove is machined round

name: scan0016-text-0747
text: the centre of its working face. No scraper rings are

name: scan0016-text-0748
text: employed. Beneath the rings seven shallow oil grooves

name: scan0016-text-0749
text: are machined circumferentially on the outside of the

name: scan0016-text-0750
text: skirt, which is not drilled at any point.

name: scan0016-text-0751
text: Fig. 6.

name: scan0016-text-0752
text: Cylinder: Section through Valve Gear.

name: scan0017-text-0754
text: CONNECTING RODS.

name: scan0017-text-0755
text: The hollow steel gudgeon pin is parallel-sided, and

name: scan0017-text-0756
text: is a push fit in the bosses, which are cast on the skirt. It is

name: scan0017-text-0757
text: located endways by the two caps shown in Fig. 8.

name: scan0017-text-0758
text: Their outer faces are radiused to the contour of the

name: scan0017-text-0759
text: cylinder walls, and they are positioned in the bosses

name: scan0017-text-0760
text: by the rectangular projections shown in the photograph.

name: scan0017-text-0761
text: They were originally fixed by spring wire clips, which

name: scan0017-text-0762
text: have since been dispensed with. The holes in their

name: scan0017-text-0763
text: centres are threaded to take an extractor. The gudgeon

name: scan0017-text-0764
text: pin is allowed to float in the piston bosses and in the

name: scan0017-text-0765
text: small end bush.

name: scan0017-text-0766
text: The connecting rods are illustrated in Fig. 9. The

name: scan0017-text-0767
text: forked rods may be fitted on either side of the engine,

name: scan0017-text-0768
text: provided that they are all assembled on the same side.

name: scan0017-text-0769
text: The forked big ends grip a split phosphor bronze shell,

name: scan0017-text-0770
text: which is fixed in them by dowel pins, whilst annular

name: scan0017-text-0771
text: grooves machined on its exterior locate the forked rods

name: scan0017-text-0772
text: and prevent them from “spreading”; the caps are not

name: scan0017-text-0773
text: bridged. The shell is lined with white metal, and works

name: scan0017-text-0774
text: on the crank-pin in the usual way. The single rod works

name: scan0017-text-0775
text: Fig. 7.

name: scan0017-text-0776
text: Broken View of “Army” Piston.

name: scan0018-text-0778
text: on the outside of the phosphor bronze shell between the

name: scan0018-text-0779
text: forked ends of the double rod. The little ends are

name: scan0018-text-0780
text: bushed with phosphor bronze. Details of the lubrication

name: scan0018-text-0781
text: are given on page 36.

name: scan0018-text-0782
text: Fig. 8.

name: scan0018-text-0783
text: Pistons and Gudgeon Pins.

name: scan0018-text-0784
text: Fig. 9.

name: scan0018-text-0785
text: Connecting Rods.

name: scan0019-text-0787
text: CRANKSHAFT.

name: scan0019-text-0788
text: The crankshaft runs in seven bearings, consisting

name: scan0019-text-0789
text: of horizontally split phosphor bronze shells, lined with

name: scan0019-text-0790
text: white metal and housed in the crosswebs of the base

name: scan0019-text-0791
text: chamber. The bearing next the propeller is 115 mm. in

name: scan0019-text-0792
text: length, and the six rear bearings are 49 mm. long. The

name: scan0019-text-0793
text: ends of the journals and crankpins are sealed on early

name: scan0019-text-0794
text: engines by brass discs, soldered into position, but the

name: scan0019-text-0795
text: standard system will consist of steel caps, drawn up by

name: scan0019-text-0796
text: bolts. Details of the lubrication are given in Chapter II.

name: scan0019-text-0797
text: The main driving bevel is machined in one piece

name: scan0019-text-0798
text: with a starting claw, and is bolted to a flange machined

name: scan0019-text-0799
text: on the rear end of the shaft. Shims are threaded over

name: scan0019-text-0800
text: the bolts between the flange and the bevel for the pur-

name: scan0019-text-0801
text: pose of adjusting the mesh of the distribution gears.

name: scan0019-text-0802
text: The centre of the bevel is internally splined to provide

name: scan0019-text-0803
text: a drive for the gun interrupter gear.

name: scan0019-text-0804
text: Fig. 85, p. 114, illustrates in detail the double thrust

name: scan0019-text-0805
text: bearing, which is located between the propeller hub taper

name: scan0019-text-0806
text: and the front main bearing, and is provided with cast

name: scan0019-text-0807
text: housings in the base chamber. Its terminal stops con-

name: scan0019-text-0808
text: sist of a flange machined on the shaft, and a large flanged

name: scan0019-text-0809
text: and castellated nut, screwing on to a thread on the shaft.

name: scan0019-text-0810
text: Fig. 10.

name: scan0019-text-0811
text: Pair of Connecting Rods (dismantled).

name: scan0020-text-0813
text: BASE CHAMBER.

name: scan0020-text-0814
text: The maximum end play should not exceed .008 in.

name: scan0020-text-0815
text: The washers locating the thrust in the crankcase are

name: scan0020-text-0816
text: thick and thin respectively. They should be selected

name: scan0020-text-0817
text: so that when assembled they leave .001 in. end play in

name: scan0020-text-0818
text: the grooves in the crankcase.

name: scan0020-text-0819
text: The propeller hub is mounted by a taper and key

name: scan0020-text-0820
text: in the usual way. The key is fixed by a grubscrew at

name: scan0020-text-0821
text: its centre, fore and aft of which there are two threaded

name: scan0020-text-0822
text: holes in the key, by means of which the grubscrew may

name: scan0020-text-0823
text: be utilised to lift the key.

name: scan0020-text-0824
text: The locking device is illustrated in Fig. 77, p. 105.

name: scan0020-text-0825
text: The base chamber is made of two aluminium alloy

name: scan0020-text-0826
text: castings bolted together: the horizontal joint comes at

name: scan0020-text-0827
text: the level of the main bearing centres, as usual. There

name: scan0020-text-0828
text: are no “feet” or bearer brackets on the upper half: its

name: scan0020-text-0829
text: flange overhangs the lower half for the full length of

name: scan0020-text-0830
text: both sides, and is attached direct to the engine bearers

name: scan0020-text-0831
text: in the fuselage by seven bolts on each side. This pro-

name: scan0020-text-0832
text: jecting flange is stiffened by seven pairs of vertical ribs

name: scan0020-text-0833
text: on both sides.

name: scan0020-text-0834
text: Fig. 11.

name: scan0020-text-0835
text: Lower Half of Main Bearing.

name: scan0020-text-0836
text: Fig. 12.

name: scan0020-text-0837
text: Crankshaft Taper and Key.

name: scan0021-text-0002
text: Fig. 13.

name: scan0021-text-0003
text: Three-quarter Side View of Engine.

name: scan0022-text-0005
text: The main bearings are housed in the cross webs, so

name: scan0022-text-0006
text: that the crankshaft can be freed by unbolting the sump.

name: scan0022-text-0007
text: Similarly, the cylinders can be removed without dis-

name: scan0022-text-0008
text: turbing the crankshaft.

name: scan0022-text-0009
text: The two parts of the base chamber are secured

name: scan0022-text-0010
text: together by fifty small bolts distributed along the flange.

name: scan0022-text-0011
text: In addition, eight pairs of heavy studs are fixed in the

name: scan0022-text-0012
text: lower half along the centre line, two pairs at the front

name: scan0022-text-0013
text: bearing, and one pair at each of the six shorter bearings;

name: scan0022-text-0014
text: and two pairs of external bolts are employed at the ex-

name: scan0022-text-0015
text: treme front and rear ends of the base chamber respec-

name: scan0022-text-0016
text: tively.

name: scan0022-text-0017
text: Fig. 14.    Top Half of Crankcase.

name: scan0022-text-0018
text: Fig. 15.    Top Half of Crankcase, viewed from beneath.

name: scan0023-text-0020
text: The top half is cross-stiffened by eight webs, which

name: scan0023-text-0021
text: incorporate tubular housings for the studs above men-

name: scan0023-text-0022
text: tioned. The rear web and the two nose piece webs are

name: scan0023-text-0023
text: solid, but the other five webs have panels cut out of

name: scan0023-text-0024
text: them. The formation of the rear end is unusual, being

name: scan0023-text-0025
text: designed to provide a moisture-proof chamber for the

name: scan0023-text-0026
text: ball bearings of the distribution gears. This chamber

name: scan0023-text-0027
text: is enclosed by means of the rear wall and top end of the

name: scan0023-text-0028
text: casting, together with solid vertical and horizontal webs.

name: scan0023-text-0029
text: In the top of the compartment so formed there are four

name: scan0023-text-0030
text: apertures, respectively closed (when the engine is

name: scan0023-text-0031
text: assembled) by a breather cap, the vertical shaft, and the

name: scan0023-text-0032
text: two inclined shafts. In the base of the compartment

name: scan0023-text-0033
text: there are two apertures, closed respectively by the vertical

name: scan0023-text-0034
text: shaft and the oil trap shown in Fig. 87, p. 116. This trap

name: scan0023-text-0035
text: is kept permanently brimming with oil, which drains into

name: scan0023-text-0036
text: it from the casings of the inclined shafts. When con-

name: scan0023-text-0037
text: densed moisture is surging about in the main base

name: scan0023-text-0038
text: chamber under the influence of crankcase compression,

name: scan0023-text-0039
text: it can find no entry into the distribution gear compart-

name: scan0023-text-0040
text: ment, seeing that the oiltrap is sealed by oil. Thus the

name: scan0023-text-0041
text: ball races within the compartment are protected from

name: scan0023-text-0042
text: rust.

name: scan0023-text-0043
text: Two large breathers are bolted to the right-hand

name: scan0023-text-0044
text: side of the upper half of the base chamber. An en-

name: scan0023-text-0045
text: graved plate on the rear end gives the firing sequence

name: scan0023-text-0046
text: of the cylinders, and the name of the manufacturer.

name: scan0023-text-0047
text: Fig. 16.

name: scan0023-text-0048
text: Bottom Half of Crankcase.

name: scan0024-text-0050
text: Fig. 17.

name: scan0024-text-0051
text: Bottom Half of Crankcase, with Crankshaft in position.

name: scan0025-text-0053
text: VALVES.

name: scan0025-text-0054
text: The lower half of the base chamber is flat-bottomed,

name: scan0025-text-0055
text: with fore and aft oil wells. It is cast with cross webs

name: scan0025-text-0056
text: at each of the six shorter main bearings, and its nose

name: scan0025-text-0057
text: piece is heavily ribbed, both laterally and longitudinally,

name: scan0025-text-0058
text: to support the front main bearing. The lower half of

name: scan0025-text-0059
text: the housing for the thrust race is cast in the nose piece.

name: scan0025-text-0060
text: Towards the rear the casting is given an approximately

name: scan0025-text-0061
text: rectangular section, and houses the drive for the oil and

name: scan0025-text-0062
text: water pumps. The base of the sump is cast with a

name: scan0025-text-0063
text: narrow trough to accommodate the main pressure oil

name: scan0025-text-0064
text: pipe and the oil return pipe from the front oil well.

name: scan0025-text-0065
text: The lower halves of the main bearings are housed

name: scan0025-text-0066
text: in the cross webs, as stated above, and are not slung

name: scan0025-text-0067
text: in caps from bolts.

name: scan0025-text-0068
text: A cylindrical housing for the plain bearing of the

name: scan0025-text-0069
text: lower vertical shaft is cast as part of the lower half at

name: scan0025-text-0070
text: the rear end, immediately below the main crankshaft

name: scan0025-text-0071
text: bevel. The water pump unit is bolted to the rear end of

name: scan0025-text-0072
text: the sump, and driven by bevel gearing off the lower vertical

name: scan0025-text-0073
text: shaft. A splined extension of this shaft drives the oil

name: scan0025-text-0074
text: pumps, the oil pump unit being bolted beneath the rear

name: scan0025-text-0075
text: end of the sump.

name: scan0025-text-0076
text: Two straight steel oil pipes are inserted from the

name: scan0025-text-0077
text: rear end, and pushed through housings in the bases of

name: scan0025-text-0078
text: the cross webs. The right-hand pipe is the main supply

name: scan0025-text-0079
text: pipe, and communicates with the bottom centre of each

name: scan0025-text-0080
text: main bearing by means of a steel pipe screwed verti-

name: scan0025-text-0081
text: cally into each web; the supply for the camshaft is taken

name: scan0025-text-0082
text: from the front main bearing through a lead in the upper

name: scan0025-text-0083
text: half of the base chamber. Screwed plugs at either end

name: scan0025-text-0084
text: facilitate the cleaning of the main pressure pipe: the

name: scan0025-text-0085
text: forward plug is beneath the sump; the rear plug is

name: scan0025-text-0086
text: visible when the pump unit is dismounted. The left-

name: scan0025-text-0087
text: hand pipe connects the forward oil well to the scavenging

name: scan0025-text-0088
text: pump in the rear oil well. The front oil well contains

name: scan0025-text-0089
text: a filter: its cover is secured by a spring clip.

name: scan0025-text-0090
text: A felt oil-retaining washer is fitted at the front of the

name: scan0025-text-0091
text: nose piece.

name: scan0025-text-0092
text: The circular orifice opposite the rear end of the

name: scan0025-text-0093
text: crankshaft may be closed by a coverplate if a gun

name: scan0025-text-0094
text: interrupter gear or mechanical starter are not fitted.

name: scan0025-text-0095
text: There are two valves per cylinder, working in cast

name: scan0025-text-0096
text: iron guides pressed into the valve pockets. The valve

name: scan0025-text-0097
text: stems are inclined towards the cylinder axis at 13

name: scan0025-text-0101
text: °, the

name: scan0025-text-0102
text: exhausts being on the outside of each cylinder block, and

name: scan0025-text-0103
text: the inlets on the inside. The camcase is accommodated

name: scan0025-text-0104
text: within the included angle. All the valves are inter-

name: scan0025-text-0105
text: changeable, their smallest diameter measuring 63.5 mm.

name: scan0026-text-0107
text: Double concentric coiled springs are fitted. The

name: scan0026-text-0108
text: inner springs are interchangeable. The outer springs of

name: scan0026-text-0109
text: the inlet valves are longer than the corresponding

name: scan0026-text-0110
text: exhaust springs, which are of stouter gauge. A female

name: scan0026-text-0111
text: taper in the upper spring cap presses a pair of internally

name: scan0026-text-0112
text: Fig. 18.

name: scan0026-text-0113
text: Valve and Fittings.

name: scan0026-text-0114
text: Fig. 19.

name: scan0026-text-0115
text: Camshaft and Bearings.

name: scan0027-text-0117
text: CAMSHAFTS AND VALVE GEAR.

name: scan0027-text-0118
text: shouldered split cones against three annular grooves

name: scan0027-text-0119
text: machined on the valve stem.

name: scan0027-text-0120
text: The camshafts are not interchangeable, and are

name: scan0027-text-0121
text: marked “R” and “L” respectively. The camcases are

name: scan0027-text-0122
text: interchangeable.

name: scan0027-text-0123
text: They are machined in one piece, and drilled for

name: scan0027-text-0124
text: pressure lubrication, of which details are printed on p. 37.

name: scan0027-text-0125
text: The driven bevel pinions are bolted to flanges on the

name: scan0027-text-0126
text: rear ends of the shafts. Notched flanges or “hubs,”

name: scan0027-text-0127
text: secured to these studs behind the bevel pinions, drive the

name: scan0027-text-0128
text: rotating portions of the distributor heads.

name: scan0027-text-0129
text: Each camshaft runs in seven bushes (see Fig. 81,

name: scan0027-text-0130
text: p. 110), which are a driving fit in the camcase. They are

name: scan0027-text-0131
text: “stepped” in outside diameter, that at the rear end

name: scan0027-text-0132
text: being the largest, the next

name: scan0027-text-0136
text: in. smaller, etc. The five

name: scan0027-text-0137
text: intermediate bearings are cast in aluminium; they are

name: scan0027-text-0138
text: horizontally split, assembled by screws, and located in

name: scan0027-text-0139
text: the camcase by large grubscrews entered from the side.

name: scan0027-text-0140
text: The front bearing of each shaft is a one-piece cylindrical

name: scan0027-text-0141
text: bush of aluminium: the oil supply enters the camshaft

name: scan0027-text-0142
text: by this bush, as described on page 38. The rear bearing

name: scan0027-text-0143
text: is of special pattern, as illustrated in Fig. 81. It con-

name: scan0027-text-0144
text: sists of two phosphor bronze shells, lined with white

name: scan0027-text-0145
text: metal, and is mounted between two flanges machined on

name: scan0027-text-0146
text: the shaft, so as to take the thrust.

name: scan0027-text-0147
text: A camcase is illustrated in Fig. 20. It is an alu-

name: scan0027-text-0148
text: minium alloy casting, of tubular section between each

name: scan0027-text-0149
text: pair of cylinders, and widening into approximately

name: scan0027-text-0150
text: rectangular compartments with detachable lids over each

name: scan0027-text-0151
text: cylinder head. It is secured to each cylinder head by

name: scan0027-text-0152
text: a couple of studs.

name: scan0027-text-0153
text: Fig. 20.

name: scan0027-text-0154
text: Camcase.

name: scan0028-text-0156
text: DISTRIBUTION GEAR.

name: scan0028-text-0157
text: The inlet and exhaust rockers are machined from

name: scan0028-text-0158
text: steel forgings, different in shape for the right- and

name: scan0028-text-0159
text: left-hand sides of the cylinders, though either shape

name: scan0028-text-0160
text: may be used to operate the inlets or the exhausts. The

name: scan0028-text-0161
text: spindles are integral with the cam and valve arms. The

name: scan0028-text-0162
text: lower half of each rocker spindle bearing is machined

name: scan0028-text-0163
text: in the camcase, and the upper half in one of the re-

name: scan0028-text-0164
text: movable lids. The spindles are located endways in

name: scan0028-text-0165
text: their bearings by the valve-actuating arm at one end,

name: scan0028-text-0166
text: and at the other end by a flange turned on the spindle.

name: scan0028-text-0167
text: Two arms project from opposite sides of each spindle.

name: scan0028-text-0168
text: A short forked arm, projecting inwards near the centre

name: scan0028-text-0169
text: of the spindle, carries a hard steel roller which engages

name: scan0028-text-0170
text: the cam. A longer arm, projecting from the end of the

name: scan0028-text-0171
text: spindle, carries an adjustable bolt which actuates the

name: scan0028-text-0172
text: valve. The bolt has a square on it, which is a loose fit

name: scan0028-text-0173
text: in a square hole at the outer end of the arm: the bolt

name: scan0028-text-0174
text: is packed to the height required for correct valve clear-

name: scan0028-text-0175
text: ance by means of shim washers, and is then locked by

name: scan0028-text-0176
text: a castellated nut and split pin. The engines are delivered

name: scan0028-text-0177
text: with three shims of different thicknesses threaded on

name: scan0028-text-0178
text: each bolt.

name: scan0028-text-0179
text: Fig. 22 is a diagram of the general layout of the dis-

name: scan0028-text-0180
text: tribution gears. The main bevel on the crankshaft

name: scan0028-text-0181
text: drives upper and lower vertical shafts. The upper

name: scan0028-text-0182
text: vertical shaft drives the two inclined shafts which form

name: scan0028-text-0183
text: the camshaft drives; and its splined extension drives the

name: scan0028-text-0184
text: low tension generator. The lower vertical shaft drives

name: scan0028-text-0185
text: the horizontal water pump shaft through bevel gearing,

name: scan0028-text-0186
text: Fig. 21.

name: scan0030-text-0236

name: scan0030-text-0237

name: scan0030-text-0238
text: A tachometer drive is taken off the generator shaft

name: scan0031-text-0264

name: scan0033-text-0296
text: OIL PUMPS.

name: scan0033-text-0297
text: The lubrication system is simple in outline, but

name: scan0033-text-0298
text: demands somewhat lengthy description, as some of the

name: scan0033-text-0299
text: individual units are complex. A large pump unit, con-

name: scan0033-text-0300
text: sisting of a three-pinion duplex scavenge pump mounted

name: scan0033-text-0301
text: above a pressure pump, is assembled in a casing bolted

name: scan0033-text-0302
text: beneath the rear end of the sump. Both pumps are

name: scan0033-text-0303
text: driven by a spindle which is jointed by splines to the

name: scan0033-text-0304
text: lower vertical shaft. The supply pump forces oil under

name: scan0033-text-0305
text: pressure along a manifold in the sump, which serves

name: scan0033-text-0306
text: all the main bearings. A lead from the front main

name: scan0033-text-0307
text: bearing conducts oil to a three-way branch at the front

name: scan0033-text-0308
text: of the base chamber, whence three pipes are connected

name: scan0033-text-0309
text: to the pressure gauge and the front ends of the two

name: scan0033-text-0310
text: camshafts respectively. The oil drains back to the sump

name: scan0033-text-0311
text: down the casings of the two inclined drives, lubricating

name: scan0033-text-0312
text: the bearings and pinions of the distribution gears on its

name: scan0033-text-0313
text: way. The pistons and gudgeon pins are lubricated by

name: scan0033-text-0314
text: splash.

name: scan0033-text-0315
text: The double scavenging pump is located in the pump

name: scan0033-text-0316
text: unit beneath the oil well at the rear end of the flat-

name: scan0033-text-0317
text: bottomed sump, and is connected by a pipe in the sump

name: scan0033-text-0318
text: to the oil well at the front end. Both oil wells are pro-

name: scan0033-text-0319
text: vided with filters, and their respective deliveries meet in

name: scan0033-text-0320
text: a common return pipe to the tank.

name: scan0033-text-0321
text: A detailed description of the various components

name: scan0033-text-0322

name: scan0033-text-0323
text: It may be found difficult to grasp all the details

name: scan0033-text-0324
text: of the pump until it has actually been dismantled; it

name: scan0033-text-0325

name: scan0033-text-0326

name: scan0033-text-0327

name: scan0033-text-0328

name: scan0033-text-0329
text: As the section in Fig. 24 shows, the double scavenge

name: scan0033-text-0330
text: pump and single pressure pump, together with the filters

name: scan0033-text-0331
text: and relief valve, are accommodated in a casing, which is

name: scan0033-text-0332

name: scan0033-text-0333
text: sure pipe and the return pipe from the front catchpit

name: scan0033-text-0334
text: are connected to the pumps via ducts drilled in the pump

name: scan0033-text-0335
text: casing. At the top of the unit is a phosphor bronze

name: scan0033-text-0336
text: bush, in which the driving spindle runs. The spindle

name: scan0033-text-0337
text: drives the centre pinion of the scavenging pump, and

name: scan0033-text-0338
text: passes through a steel partition into the driven pinion of

name: scan0033-text-0339
text: the lower or pressure pump. The loose gears are

name: scan0034-text-0341
text: mounted on steel spindles fixed in the casing. The oil

name: scan0034-text-0342
text: is filtered before entering either pump: the upper filter

name: scan0034-text-0343
text: is locked in position by a nut and tab washer: the lower

name: scan0034-text-0344
text: filter is secured by the bottom cover. The relief valve

name: scan0034-text-0345
text: is situated immediately outside the delivery port of the

name: scan0034-text-0346
text: pressure pump.

text: Fig. 25 is purely diagrammatic, and does not show

name: scan0034-text-0348

name: scan0034-text-0350

name: scan0034-text-0351

name: scan0034-text-0352
text: the pump at C, and enters the sump pressure manifold

name: scan0034-text-0353
text: at C1, passing on its way the relief valve D.

name: scan0034-text-0354
text: Turning to the scavenge pump, it must be remem-

name: scan0034-text-0355

name: scan0034-text-0356
text: aeroplane is diving or climbing, the drainage oil will run

name: scan0034-text-0357
text: exclusively into the front or rear oil well. The scavenge

name: scan0034-text-0358
text: pump consists of three pinions, driven by the centre

name: scan0034-text-0359
text: gear. It is therefore the equivalent of two separate

name: scan0034-text-0360
text: pumps, each composed of two gears: as its gears have

name: scan0034-text-0361
text: deeper teeth than the gears of the pressure pump, each

name: scan0034-text-0362
text: of its units is singly more powerful than the supply

name: scan0034-text-0363
text: pump.

name: scan0038-text-0398
text: As there is a popular impression that gear pumps

name: scan0038-text-0399
text: will not exert strong suction, it may be of interest to

name: scan0038-text-0400
text: state that they suck oil quite efficiently over a much

name: scan0038-text-0401
text: greater distance than is required in this engine: but they

name: scan0038-text-0402
text: will only suck when they are primed. The two scavenge

name: scan0038-text-0403
text: pumps being formed of only three gear wheels, which-

name: scan0038-text-0404
text: ever pair is working at any moment keeps the remaining

name: scan0038-text-0405

name: scan0038-text-0411

name: scan0038-text-0412
text: in the casing of the scavenge pump, crossing over the

name: scan0038-text-0413
text: top of the pump from one side to the other.

name: scan0038-text-0414
text: The relief valve is of the mushroom type; when an

name: scan0038-text-0415

name: scan0038-text-0416

name: scan0038-text-0417

name: scan0038-text-0418
text: The bottom of the sump is cast with a narrow trough

name: scan0038-text-0420

name: scan0038-text-0421

name: scan0038-text-0422
text: is pushed in from the rear end of the sump, and provided

name: scan0038-text-0423

name: scan0038-text-0424
text: be cleansed. Vertical branch pipes, screwed into each of

name: scan0038-text-0425
text: the cross webs, connect it with the bottom centres of

name: scan0038-text-0426
text: the main bearings, in which the oil is distributed by suit-

name: scan0038-text-0427
text: able grooves, a supply being trapped by milled notches

name: scan0038-text-0428
text: in the white metal along the joints of the bearing on both

name: scan0038-text-0429
text: sides. At each bearing some of the oil enters the

name: scan0038-text-0430
text: crankshaft through a suitable hole, travels up the

name: scan0038-text-0431
text: rear web of the throw into the crank-pin, and is forced

name: scan0038-text-0432

name: scan0038-text-0433
text: grooves distribute oil over the crank-pin bearing, and

name: scan0039-text-0438

name: scan0039-text-0439
text: which the single connecting rod oscillates.

name: scan0039-text-0440
text: The ends of the journals and crank-pins are sealed

name: scan0039-text-0441

name: scan0039-text-0442
text: engines will have steel plugs drawn up by bolts.

name: scan0040-text-0466
text: cap, beneath which there is a C.A. washer: the oil pipe

name: scan0040-text-0467
text: is connected to the centre of the cap. The front cam-

name: scan0040-text-0468
text: shaft bearing is a cylindrical bush of aluminium: its

name: scan0040-text-0469
text: front end is sealed by a metal plate, attached to the bush

name: scan0040-text-0470
text: by four screws, and rendered oiltight by a paper washer.

name: scan0040-text-0471
text: Thus an oil recess is formed between the metal plate

name: scan0040-text-0472
text: and the screwed cap already mentioned. An oil duct is

name: scan0040-text-0473
text: machined in the thickness of the cylindrical bush, parallel

name: scan0040-text-0474
text: with its axis. The front end of this duct is open to the

name: scan0040-text-0475
text: oil chamber; the rear end of the duct turns at right-

name: scan0040-text-0476
text: angles, and opens into the centre of the bush, where it

name: scan0040-text-0477
text: registers once in each revolution with a hole drilled

name: scan0040-text-0478
text: through into the centre of the hollow camshaft. Oil

name: scan0040-text-0479
text: under pressure thus enters the camshaft, and is sprayed

name: scan0040-text-0480
text: out of holes positioned at the centres of the six remaining

name: scan0040-text-0481
text: bearings, along which it is distributed by suitable grooves.

name: scan0040-text-0482
text: There are no oil exits from the camshaft in the cam

name: scan0040-text-0483
text: compartments, but an ample supply of oil leaks along

name: scan0040-text-0484
text: the bearings into each compartment, and is splashed up

name: scan0040-text-0485

name: scan0040-text-0487

name: scan0040-text-0488

name: scan0040-text-0489

name: scan0040-text-0490

name: scan0040-text-0491
text: the spindle bearing through the oil exits above men-

name: scan0040-text-0492
text: tioned.

text: As described in a previous chapter, the compartment

text: The main thrust bearing is lubricated by surplus oil

text: is provided on the top of the nose piece, and the thrust

name: scan0044-text-0045
text: Carburation.

name: scan0044-text-0046
text: Two duplex carburettors are bolted beneath the

name: scan0044-text-0047
text: junctions of the forward and rear pairs of induction

name: scan0044-text-0048
text: manifolds respectively, American Zeniths, type 52 D.F.

name: scan0044-text-0049
text: being fitted to some engines, and Claudel-Hobsons

name: scan0044-text-0050

name: scan0045-text-0055
text: Zenith Carburettors.

name: scan0045-text-0056
text: Examination of these carburettors will show that

name: scan0045-text-0057
text: they have been modified in this country as the altitude

name: scan0045-text-0058
text: control originally fitted was not satisfactory. The

name: scan0045-text-0059
text: general functioning of the carburettor has also been

name: scan0045-text-0060
text: much improved.

name: scan0045-text-0061
text: Each carburettor is built up of three castings, viz.,

name: scan0045-text-0062
text: a throttle chamber, a main casting embodying duplex

name: scan0045-text-0063
text: mixing chambers, together with a single float chamber,

name: scan0045-text-0064
text: and an air intake. The latter is quickly detachable, being

name: scan0045-text-0065
text: secured by spring clips to a couple of studs on the sides

name: scan0045-text-0066
text: of the main casting. The throttle chamber contains a

name: scan0045-text-0067
text: pair of butterfly throttle valves.

name: scan0045-text-0068
text: The maintenance of an approximately constant

name: scan0045-text-0069
text: petrol-air ratio at all engine speeds is attained by the

name: scan0045-text-0070
text: familiar Zenith device of a compensating jet. If petrol

name: scan0045-text-0071
text: is supplied by a single jet located in the centre of a choke

name: scan0045-text-0072
text: tube, high engine speeds will result in an excessive flow

name: scan0045-text-0073
text: of petrol, due partly to the inertia of the column of

name: scan0045-text-0074
text: petrol, and partly to the increased depression or suction.

name: scan0045-text-0075
text: Conversely, there will be a deficiency of petrol at low

name: scan0045-text-0076
text: speeds, owing to the weakness of the depression round

name: scan0045-text-0077
text: the jet, and the low momentum of the stream of petrol

name: scan0045-text-0078
text: between the float chamber and the jet. The com-

name: scan0045-text-0079
text: pensating jet corrects these faults, because it possesses

name: scan0045-text-0080
text: exactly opposite tendencies, supplying an excess of petrol

name: scan0045-text-0081
text: at low speeds, and a reduced quantity of petrol at high

name: scan0045-text-0082
text: speeds. Consequently, if the main and compensating

name: scan0045-text-0083
text: jets are properly balanced, they co-operate to furnish a

name: scan0045-text-0084
text: correct flow at all speeds.

name: scan0047-text-0122
text: Fig. 37 is a diagrammatic sketch of the Zenith

name: scan0047-text-0123
text: principle in a simple form. G is the main jet, drawing

name: scan0047-text-0124
text: petrol from the float chamber in the usual way. I is the

name: scan0047-text-0125
text: compensator, or compensating jet, which controls the

name: scan0047-text-0126
text: flow of petrol from the float chamber into the well J. The

name: scan0047-text-0127
text: well J supplies petrol to a secondary spraying tube H

name: scan0047-text-0128
text: parallel to the main jet G. It is clear that the flow of

name: scan0047-text-0129
text: petrol from H will depend upon the height of the column

name: scan0047-text-0130
text: of petrol in J, and this depends solely on the amount of

name: scan0047-text-0131
text: petrol which can pass the compensating orifice I in a

name: scan0047-text-0132
text: given time. The hole at I, namely the orifice of the

name: scan0047-text-0133
text: compensating jet, is much smaller than the bore of the

name: scan0047-text-0134
text: passage which supplies petrol to the main jet G. When

name: scan0047-text-0135
text: the engine is not working, petrol rises in J, and a maxi-

name: scan0047-text-0136
text: mum flow is ensured from H for starting purposes.

name: scan0047-text-0137
text: When the engine is running slowly, a maximum supply is

name: scan0047-text-0138
text: obtainable from H, which balances the minimum supply

name: scan0047-text-0139
text: drawn from G by the depression. When the engine is

name: scan0047-text-0140
text: running at full speed, a minimum supply will reach H,

name: scan0047-text-0141
text: whereas the increase in the depression is drawing a

name: scan0047-text-0142
text: maximum supply from G. The action of the two jets

name: scan0047-text-0143
text: is therefore mutually opposed: and if the orifices at I

name: scan0047-text-0144
text: and G are accurately calibrated, a predetermined petrol-

name: scan0047-text-0145
text: air ratio can be ensured at all engine speeds.

name: scan0047-text-0146
text: Fig. 38 gives a sectioned view of the application of this

name: scan0047-text-0147
text: principle employed in the American Zenith carburettor,

name: scan0047-text-0148
text: type 52 D.F., as fitted to some of the Liberty engines.

name: scan0047-text-0149
text: H is the main jet. Its petrol supply is received direct

name: scan0047-text-0150
text: from the float chamber via the ducts D and F, and is

name: scan0047-text-0151
text: mainly conditioned by the depression in the mixing cham-

name: scan0047-text-0152
text: ber. The jet H delivers its minimum flow of petrol at

name: scan0047-text-0153
text: low engine speeds, and its maximum flow at full throttle

name: scan0047-text-0154
text: openings.

name: scan0047-text-0155
text: The main jet H is balanced by the outer or “shroud”

name: scan0047-text-0156
text: tube I, which surrounds H concentrically. The tube I

name: scan0047-text-0157
text: receives its supply of petrol from the well Y, which in

name: scan0047-text-0158
text: turn is supplied via the compensating orifice or jet in the

name: scan0047-text-0159
text: plug E. Thus the supply of petrol to the tube I is not

name: scan0047-text-0160
text: conditioned by the depression in the mixing chamber,

name: scan0047-text-0161
text: but by the calibrated orifice in the plug E (i.e., the com-

name: scan0047-text-0162
text: pensating jet). When the engine is running slowly, the

name: scan0047-text-0163
text: petrol flowing through the compensator E will build up

name: scan0047-text-0164
text: to a comparatively high level in the well Y: as the

name: scan0047-text-0165
text: engine is accelerated, the petrol level in Y will sink.

name: scan0047-text-0166
text: Consequently, a maximum flow of petrol is drawn from

name: scan0047-text-0167
text: the tube I at low engine speeds, and a minimum flow

name: scan0047-text-0168
text: at high speeds. Thus its action is directly opposed to

name: scan0047-text-0169
text: that of the main jet H; the main jet and compensator

name: scan0047-text-0170
text: balance each other, and co-operate to supply an approxi-

name: scan0047-text-0171
text: mately constant petrol: air ratio at all engine speeds.

name: scan0048-text-0173
text: The slow-running device is in duplicate. Each con-

name: scan0048-text-0174
text: sists of a tube M dipping at its lower end into the petrol

name: scan0048-text-0175
text: in the well Y and connected at its upper end by the small

name: scan0048-text-0176
text: duct N to the throttle chamber, into which it opens on a

name: scan0048-text-0177
text: level with the lower edge of the butterfly throttle, when

name: scan0048-text-0178
text: the latter is almost shut. With the throttle in its mini-

name: scan0048-text-0179
text: mum position, the depression is insufficient to bring the

name: scan0048-text-0180
text: jets H and I into action, but is concentrated upon the

name: scan0048-text-0181
text: mouth of the slow-running by-pass at N¹. Petrol is drawn

name: scan0048-text-0182
text: up the dipping tube through the pilot jet at X and mixed

name: scan0048-text-0183
text: with air inhaled at K.

name: scan0048-text-0184
text: No adjustments to the main spraying devices are

name: scan0048-text-0185
text: possible or necessary, the choke tubes, the main jets H

name: scan0048-text-0186
text: and the compensators I, being standard calibrated sizes

name: scan0048-text-0187
text: for all Liberty engines.

name: scan0048-text-0188
text: A throttle stop, controlling the quantity adjustment

name: scan0048-text-0189
text: for slow running, is located beneath the throttle control

name: scan0048-text-0190
text: spindle. (See pp. 142—3 for important note on adjusting

name: scan0048-text-0191
text: the carburettor controls.)

name: scan0048-text-0192
text: Both throttles are operated by a single lever through

name: scan0048-text-0193
text: a pair of toothed quadrants.

name: scan0050-text-0204
text: THE ALTITUDE CONTROL.

name: scan0050-text-0205
text: The official Zenith jets for the Liberty engine are :—

name: scan0050-text-0206
text: The density of the air decreases rapidly within the

name: scan0050-text-0207
text: altitudes now reached by aeroplanes. The deficiency of

name: scan0050-text-0208
text: oxygen then results in an over rich mixture, which is

name: scan0050-text-0209
text: corrected by reducing the flow of petrol in proportion to

name: scan0050-text-0210
text: altitude. This correction is effected by the pilot at his

name: scan0050-text-0211
text: discretion by means of a separate control lever. On the

name: scan0050-text-0212
text: carburettor under notice the “vacuum” system is em-

name: scan0050-text-0213
text: ployed. The flow of petrol from the float chamber to

name: scan0050-text-0214
text: the main jet depends upon a difference between the

name: scan0050-text-0215
text: pressure ruling in the float and mixing chambers respec-

name: scan0050-text-0216
text: tively. Whereas the float chamber is subject to atmos-

name: scan0050-text-0217
text: pheric pressure, the mixing chamber is governed by a

name: scan0050-text-0218
text: “depression,” which may alternatively be described as

name: scan0050-text-0219
text: a partial vacuum, due to the descent of the pistons in the

name: scan0050-text-0220
text: cylinders of the engine. Thus, if the petrol in the car-

name: scan0050-text-0221
text: burettor be regarded as a U-shaped column, there is

name: scan0050-text-0222
text: atmospheric pressure at the float chamber tip of the U,

name: scan0050-text-0223
text: and a depression at the mixing chamber tip of the U.

name: scan0050-text-0224
text: The flow of petrol depends upon the difference between

name: scan0050-text-0225
text: these two pressures. It is thus a simple matter to cut

name: scan0050-text-0226
text: down the supply of petrol at high altitudes by reducing

name: scan0050-text-0227
text: the pressure in the float chamber. Under the vacuum

name: scan0050-text-0228
text: system of altitude control, the float chamber is fitted

name: scan0050-text-0229
text: with an airtight lid, and is supplied with air at ground

name: scan0050-text-0230
text: level and at moderate altitudes through a small hole

name: scan0050-text-0231
text: communicating with the atmosphere and termed a “leak

name: scan0050-text-0232
text: hole.” So long as the leak hole alone is in action,

name: scan0050-text-0233
text: atmospheric pressure governs the float chamber, and the

name: scan0050-text-0234
text: maximum supply of petrol is assured. As the aeroplane

name: scan0050-text-0235
text: gains altitude, and the petrol supply becomes excessive, the

name: scan0050-text-0236
text: control cock is operated to connect up a “suction hole”

name: scan0050-text-0237
text: with the float chamber. This suction hole draws air

name: scan0050-text-0238
text: to the depression area at the narrowest diameter of

name: scan0050-text-0239
text: the choke tube: the pressure in the float chamber is

name: scan0050-text-0240
text: proportionately reduced, and the petrol supply is cut

name: scan0050-text-0241
text: down.

name: scan0050-text-0242
text: The details of the control on this type of Zenith

name: scan0050-text-0243
text: carburettor have been modified for the British Services,

name: scan0050-text-0244
text: and are shown in Figs. 38 and 42. The bridge piece

name: scan0050-text-0245
text: between the choke tubes contains a hollow chamber,

name: scan0050-text-0246
text: connected as follows:—

name: scan0050-text-0247
text: Choke Tube

name: scan0050-text-0248
text: 36 mm.

name: scan0050-text-0249
text: Main Jet

name: scan0050-text-0251
text: Compensator

name: scan0050-text-0253
text: Shroud Tube

name: scan0050-text-0254
text: 3.9 mm. diameter.

name: scan0051-text-0256
text: Claudel-Hobson Carburettor,

name: scan0051-text-0257
text: Type H.C. 7.

name: scan0051-text-0258
text: i. By the hole P to the float chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0259
text: ii. By the pipe O to the main air intake. This

name: scan0051-text-0260
text: pipe O is the “leakhole.”

name: scan0051-text-0261
text: iii. By the duct Q to the housing of the altitude

name: scan0051-text-0262
text: control cock, from which the “suction holes”

name: scan0051-text-0263
text: R open into the mixing chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0264
text: The pipe or leakhole O is permanently open. So long

name: scan0051-text-0265
text: as the suction holes R are closed by the altitude control

name: scan0051-text-0266
text: cock, O forms the sole air supply to the float chamber,

name: scan0051-text-0267
text: and the flow of petrol to the main jet is at its maximum.

name: scan0051-text-0268
text: As the control cock is progressively operated to open up

name: scan0051-text-0269
text: the suction holes R, the pressure in the float chamber

name: scan0051-text-0270
text: is weakened, and the flow of petrol to the jet is reduced.

name: scan0051-text-0271
text: This carburettor aims at providing a predetermined

name: scan0051-text-0272
text: petrol-air ratio over the full range of engine speeds by a

name: scan0051-text-0273
text: principle quite different to that employed in the Zenith.

name: scan0051-text-0274
text: In outline the system is as follows:—

name: scan0051-text-0275
text: (a) Throttle shut to slow-running position. The

name: scan0051-text-0276
text: petrol supply is restricted by a calibrated

name: scan0051-text-0277
text: pilot jet: the air supply is automatically

name: scan0051-text-0278
text: Fig. 42.

name: scan0051-text-0279
text: Diagram illustrating Zenith Altitude Control.

name: scan0051-text-0280
text: O—Leakhole.

name: scan0051-text-0281
text: P—Lead to float chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0282
text: R—Suction hole.

name: scan0052-text-0284
text: restricted by the slow speed of the engine:

name: scan0052-text-0285
text: indeed, the velocity of the air would be too

name: scan0052-text-0286
text: low to pick up petrol if the air were not

name: scan0052-text-0287
text: drawn through narrow passages, e.g., a

name: scan0052-text-0288
text: strangling slot in the throttle barrel, and a

name: scan0052-text-0289
text: small bore by-pass: these narrow passages

name: scan0052-text-0290
text: increase the velocity of the air stream.

name: scan0052-text-0291
text: (b) Full throttle opening. The petrol supply is

name: scan0052-text-0292
text: determined by a calibrated main jet of the

name: scan0052-text-0293
text: submerged type, mounted at the base of a

name: scan0052-text-0294
text: “diffuser” in the mixing chamber. The

name: scan0052-text-0295
text: volume and velocity of the air stream are

name: scan0052-text-0296
text: conditioned by the diameter of the choke

name: scan0052-text-0297
text: tube, etc.

name: scan0052-text-0298
text: Fig. 43.

name: scan0052-text-0299
text: H.C. 7 Duplex Carburettor.

name: scan0053-text-0301
text: (c) Intermediate throttle openings. As ex-

name: scan0053-text-0302
text: plained on page 43, the tendency of a crude

name: scan0053-text-0303
text: carburettor is to supply an excess of petrol

name: scan0053-text-0304
text: when the depression or suction reaches a

name: scan0053-text-0305
text: maximum at high engine speeds. This ten-

name: scan0053-text-0306
text: dency is counteracted in the H.C. 7 by the

name: scan0053-text-0307
text: calibrated main jet; its maximum delivery

name: scan0053-text-0308
text: is correct for high engine speeds. Such a

name: scan0053-text-0309
text: system introduces a fresh difficulty. If the

name: scan0053-text-0310
text: petrol supply is correct at full speed, it is

name: scan0053-text-0311
text: likely to be deficient at quarter, half, and

name: scan0053-text-0312
text: three-quarter throttle openings, when the

name: scan0053-text-0313
text: depression is less. This difficulty is over-

name: scan0053-text-0314
text: come by employing a varying petrol level

name: scan0053-text-0315
text: in the diffuser tube. At intermediate

name: scan0053-text-0316
text: speeds the main jet passes slightly more

name: scan0053-text-0317
text: petrol than can be atomised. This small

name: scan0053-text-0318
text: surplus of spirit forms a reserve in the

name: scan0053-text-0319
text: diffuser, and the amount of the reserve will

name: scan0053-text-0320
text: vary in proportion to the engine speed. As

name: scan0053-text-0321
text: the diffuser is formed from tubes of small

name: scan0053-text-0322
text: diameter, the level of the petrol in the

name: scan0053-text-0323
text: diffuser will also vary. As the level falls,

name: scan0053-text-0324
text: the main jet is progressively relieved of

name: scan0053-text-0325
text: suction by air entering through the holes

name: scan0053-text-0326
text: in the diffuser tube.

name: scan0053-text-0327
text: Consequently, as the engine is acceler-

name: scan0053-text-0328
text: ated from its minimum towards its maxi-

name: scan0053-text-0329
text: mum speed, the petrol level is gradually

name: scan0053-text-0330
text: and automatically lowered by the depletion

name: scan0053-text-0331
text: of the reserve in the diffuser tubes; and,

name: scan0053-text-0332
text: contrariwise, as the engine is slowed down,

name: scan0053-text-0333
text: the reserve is built up again, and the level

name: scan0053-text-0334
text: rises. Thus the tendency of an increasing

name: scan0053-text-0335
text: depression to enrich the mixture is counter-

name: scan0053-text-0336
text: acted, and vice versâ.

name: scan0053-text-0337
text: The diffuser tube also serves a further purpose.

name: scan0053-text-0338
text: In carburettors fitted with a simple jet, a stream of pure

name: scan0053-text-0339
text: petrol issues from the top of the jet, and is not mixed

name: scan0053-text-0340
text: with air until it enters the choke tube. With a diffuser

name: scan0053-text-0341
text: type of jet, a small quantity of air is drawn at high

name: scan0053-text-0342
text: velocity through the jet, and is mixed with the petrol

name: scan0053-text-0343
text: before the latter issues into the choke tube. (The quan-

name: scan0053-text-0344
text: tity of air depends upon the number of air holes in the

name: scan0053-text-0345
text: diffuser tube uncovered by the falling petrol level.) Thus,

name: scan0053-text-0346
text: instead of delivering pure petrol, the diffuser sprays out

name: scan0053-text-0347
text: an “emulsion” of mingled petrol vapour and air into

name: scan0053-text-0348
text: the stream of air drawn up from the main intake. This

name: scan0053-text-0349
text: emulsion impinges into the main air stream at high speed,

name: scan0054-text-0351
text: and at a sharp angle; atomisation is consequently

name: scan0054-text-0352
text: thorough.

name: scan0054-text-0353
text: The sectional drawing, Fig. 44, and the photograph,

name: scan0054-text-0354

name: scan0054-text-0355

name: scan0054-text-0356

name: scan0054-text-0357

name: scan0054-text-0358
text: as an air strangler, concentrating the depression round

name: scan0054-text-0359
text: the head of the tube. The slow-running mixture is drawn

name: scan0054-text-0360
text: into the engine partly via the by-pass shown in Fig. 44,

name: scan0054-text-0361
text: and partly through the V in the back of the throttle.

text: The diffuser is illustrated in Figs. 46, 47. Petrol

name: scan0055-text-0368
text: passes through the main jet A into the base of the diffu-

name: scan0055-text-0369
text: ser: the main jet A determines the rate of the

name: scan0055-text-0370
text: petrol supply, and its effective diameter must on

name: scan0055-text-0371
text: no account be tampered with, e.g., by cleaning

name: scan0055-text-0372
text: with a broach. The petrol then fills the three concentric

name: scan0055-text-0373
text: tubes B, N and M to a maximum height, determined

name: scan0055-text-0374
text: by the adjustment of the float needle. This maximum

name: scan0055-text-0375
text: height will be set at 8 mm. below the lip of the “guard”

name: scan0055-text-0376
text: tube M; other considerations, as is explained below,

name: scan0055-text-0377
text: affect the level while the engine is running. The action

name: scan0055-text-0378
text: of these tubes will now be described in detail.

name: scan0055-text-0379
text: The Slow-Running Tube B.—The slow-running tube

name: scan0055-text-0380
text: B is mounted in series with the main jet A, i.e., it

name: scan0055-text-0381
text: receives its petrol supply via A and D, instead of through

name: scan0055-text-0382
text: a separate duct: the method of supply makes for fuel

name: scan0055-text-0383
text: economy, as B tends to go out of action when the

name: scan0055-text-0384
text: throttle is opened. A constriction in the inner diameter

name: scan0055-text-0385
text: of B at the point X forms the pilot jet. There are two

name: scan0055-text-0386
text: separate air supplies for slow-running purposes. Air

name: scan0055-text-0387
text: from the main intake enters the “air” tube P through

name: scan0055-text-0388
text: the holes H, passes up P, over the lip of the “guard” tube

name: scan0055-text-0389
text: Fig. 46.

name: scan0055-text-0390
text: Section of the H.C. 7 Diffuser.

name: scan0056-text-0392
text: M, and through the depression holes F F into the

name: scan0056-text-0393
text: “diffuser” tube N. From N the air passes into the slow-

name: scan0056-text-0394
text: running tube B via the holes E E, immediately above the

name: scan0056-text-0395
text: pilot jet X. This air is mixed with petrol before it

name: scan0056-text-0396
text: emerges from the head of tube B. A second air supply

name: scan0056-text-0397
text: is drawn up through the main air intake, its velocity being

name: scan0056-text-0398
text: greatly increased by the strangler slot in the throttle

name: scan0056-text-0399
text: barrel, which slides down round the top of B in the closed

name: scan0056-text-0400
text: position of the throttle. The slow-running mixture

name: scan0056-text-0401
text: passes towards the engine through the by-pass shown in

name: scan0056-text-0402
text: Fig. 44, which is adjustable by means of a screw.

name: scan0056-text-0403
text: The main jet A passes more petrol than can be

name: scan0056-text-0404
text: atomised through the tube B. Consequently, while the

name: scan0056-text-0405
text: engine is running slowly, the tubes N and M fill up with

name: scan0056-text-0406
text: petrol to the fixed maximum level, in readiness for the

name: scan0056-text-0407
text: liberal supply of petrol required for acceleration.

name: scan0056-text-0408
text: The Depression Tube N.—On the throttle being

name: scan0056-text-0409
text: opened, the depression immediately begins to act upon

name: scan0056-text-0410
text: the depression tube N through the emulsion holes G G.

name: scan0056-text-0411
text: Petrol is drawn out through G G, and is already mixed

name: scan0056-text-0412
text: with air drawn through the diffuser holes F F, over the

name: scan0056-text-0413
text: lip of the guard tube M, out of the air tube P. This air

name: scan0056-text-0414
text: and petrol are already mixed together when they emerge

name: scan0056-text-0415
text: from G G, and impinge upon the stream of air drawn

name: scan0056-text-0416
text: up outside the diffuser from the main intake.

name: scan0056-text-0417
text: Fig. 47.

name: scan0056-text-0418
text: Parts of the Diffuser (shown dismantled).

name: scan0057-text-0420
text: As the engine speed rises there would be a tendency

name: scan0057-text-0421
text: for an excessive amount of petrol to be atomised, if the

name: scan0057-text-0422
text: level in the diffuser remained constant. But the main

name: scan0057-text-0423
text: jet A is not large enough to maintain the maximum level

name: scan0057-text-0424
text: of petrol in the tubes M, N, and B permanently; so the

name: scan0057-text-0425
text: mixture remains constant.

name: scan0057-text-0426
text: If the engine is throttled right down again, the slow-

name: scan0057-text-0427
text: running tube B comes into action afresh, and a reserve

name: scan0057-text-0428
text: of petrol again accumulates in M and N.

name: scan0057-text-0429
text: The guard tube M is obviously provided to retain

name: scan0057-text-0430
text: petrol in the depression tube N, whilst allowing air to

name: scan0057-text-0431
text: enter N at the holes F F: it is essential that some of the

name: scan0057-text-0432
text: holes F F shall be near the surface of the petrol at all

name: scan0057-text-0433
text: its varying levels, so that they are drilled at intervals

name: scan0057-text-0434
text: from the bottom to the top.

name: scan0057-text-0435
text: The air tube P increases the velocity of the air which

name: scan0057-text-0436
text: is drawn through the diffuser.

name: scan0057-text-0437
text: (Readers familiar with the earlier issues of the H.C. 7

name: scan0057-text-0438
text: type should note that no air cones are now fitted round

name: scan0057-text-0439
text: the diffuser.)

name: scan0057-text-0440
text: Adjustments.—No adjustments to the diffuser assem-

name: scan0057-text-0441
text: bly are possible or desirable, as its working depends

name: scan0057-text-0442
text: upon a variety of orifices, all of which are calibrated.

name: scan0057-text-0443
text: Nor must any attempt be made to dismantle the unit

name: scan0057-text-0444
text: consisting of tubes N, M and P. The tube N is expanded

name: scan0057-text-0445
text: into position, and the parts are soldered together: any

name: scan0057-text-0446
text: tampering will merely result in wrecking the assembly.

name: scan0057-text-0447
text: Cleaning should be done by blowing through, and not

name: scan0057-text-0448
text: with broaches. The sole permissible adjustment which

name: scan0057-text-0449
text: affects the diffuser, is the setting of the petrol level,

name: scan0057-text-0450
text: which should be kept at 8 mm. below the lip of the tube

name: scan0057-text-0451
text: M: the collar is a tapping fit on the float needle, to

name: scan0057-text-0452
text: which it is lightly soldered after setting.

name: scan0057-text-0453
text: The slow-running mixture can be adjusted for quan-

name: scan0057-text-0454
text: tity by setting the adjusting screw of the by-pass

name: scan0057-text-0455
text: (Fig. 44); and for quality, by setting the adjustable

name: scan0057-text-0456
text: throttle stop screw. It might appear that the latter

name: scan0057-text-0457
text: would only affect the quantity of the mixture; but it

name: scan0057-text-0458
text: governs the strangling effect of the throttle slot round

name: scan0057-text-0459
text: the head of tube B, and so varies the quality.

name: scan0057-text-0460
text: These adjustments will usually repay trouble after

name: scan0057-text-0461
text: an engine has been overhauled, as the sum total of the

name: scan0057-text-0462
text: air leaks at the various joints in the induction system

name: scan0057-text-0463
text: must inevitably vary. The adjustment should be made

name: scan0057-text-0464
text: with the engine warm, as its purpose is not so much to

name: scan0057-text-0465
text: secure the best starting adjustment, as to obtain an

name: scan0057-text-0466
text: economical setting on which an engine can be trusted

name: scan0057-text-0467
text: not to choke when throttled down during flight. The

name: scan0057-text-0468
text: procedure is therefore as follows:—

name: scan0058-text-0470
text: FITTING NOTES.

name: scan0058-text-0471
text: i. Warm up the engine.

name: scan0058-text-0472
text: ii. Set the throttle stop, till the engine just keeps

name: scan0058-text-0473
text: running, and no more.

name: scan0058-text-0474
text: iii. Unscrew the by-pass adjustment a little, so

name: scan0058-text-0475
text: that the engine runs a shade faster.

name: scan0058-text-0476
text: iv. Slow the engine down a little by resetting the

name: scan0058-text-0477
text: throttle stop.

name: scan0058-text-0478
text: By the above method, the desired minimum engine

name: scan0058-text-0479
text: speed is attained, plus a little extra strangling of the air,

name: scan0058-text-0480
text: which will facilitate starting.

name: scan0058-text-0481
text: The standard Claudel jet sizes for the Liberty engine

name: scan0058-text-0482
text: are:—

name: scan0058-text-0483
text: If a light carburettor is bolted up to an untrue

name: scan0058-text-0484
text: induction pipe flange, the carburettor body may be dis-

name: scan0058-text-0485
text: torted, and the throttle will bind. It is therefore

name: scan0058-text-0486
text: essential to ensure a true jointing face on the induction

name: scan0058-text-0487
text: manifold. This is peculiarly difficult with the Liberty

name: scan0058-text-0488
text: engine, on which one carburettor face beds against ports

name: scan0058-text-0489
text: in two separate induction manifolds: and the need for

name: scan0058-text-0490
text: extreme care in erecting the cylinders and their mani-

name: scan0058-text-0491
text: folds is indicated.

name: scan0058-text-0492
text: Thin fibre washers are exclusively used for jointing,

name: scan0058-text-0493
text: except at the joint between the two halves of the car-

name: scan0058-text-0494
text: burettor, where a thin (.01 in. maximum) paper washer is

name: scan0058-text-0495
text: employed.

name: scan0058-text-0496
text: The main jet must make a petrol tight joint with its

name: scan0058-text-0497
text: seating, or the calibration of the jet becomes futile.

name: scan0058-text-0498
text: The movement of the altitude control lever is short,

name: scan0058-text-0499
text: owing to the limited travel of the small cock; the

name: scan0058-text-0500
text: leverage should therefore be multiplied in linking this

name: scan0058-text-0501
text: lever to the cock it controls.

name: scan0058-text-0502
text: Care must be taken to synchronise the controls, so

name: scan0058-text-0503
text: that movements of the cockpit levers affect both car-

name: scan0058-text-0504
text: burettors identically: this, of course, applies to the alti-

name: scan0058-text-0505
text: tude controls as well as to the throttles. Spare vacuum

name: scan0058-text-0506
text: cocks are interchangeable, in the event of wear or

name: scan0058-text-0507
text: damage. Under no circumstances must the holes or

name: scan0058-text-0508
text: slots be tampered with in squadrons.

name: scan0058-text-0509
text: If the petrol is pressure-fed, the relief valve must

name: scan0058-text-0510
text: act at 3 lbs. per square inch (absolute maximum). If

name: scan0058-text-0511
text: fuel is fed by gravity, the head must not be less than

name: scan0058-text-0512
text: two feet.

name: scan0059-text-0518
text: POSSIBLE CAUSES OF TROUBLE.

name: scan0059-text-0519
text: THE ALTITUDE CONTROL.

name: scan0059-text-0520
text: I. Absence or Shortage of Petrol.

name: scan0059-text-0521
text: 1. Choked jets. Clear by blowing; the use of

name: scan0059-text-0522
text: broaches is forbidden.

name: scan0059-text-0523
text: 2. Dirt in tanks, supply piping, or filter.

name: scan0059-text-0524
text: 3. Air lock in supply piping.

name: scan0059-text-0525
text: 4. Needle valve stuck.

name: scan0059-text-0526
text: 5. Toggle levers jambed.

name: scan0059-text-0527
text: 6. Empty tanks.

name: scan0059-text-0528
text: 7. Excessive heat, producing vapour lock in

name: scan0059-text-0529
text: supply pipe.

name: scan0059-text-0530
text: II. Excess of Petrol: “Flooding.”

name: scan0059-text-0531
text: 1. Damaged, bent, worn, or eccentric needle.

name: scan0059-text-0532
text: 2. Faulty needle seating (removable without dis-

name: scan0059-text-0533
text: mantling carburettor).

name: scan0059-text-0534
text: 3. Damaged washers on jet or needle seatings.

name: scan0059-text-0535
text: 4. Other forms of leak at main jet seating.

name: scan0059-text-0536
text: 5. Petrol level too high.

name: scan0059-text-0537
text: 6. Toggle levers jambed.

name: scan0059-text-0538
text: 7. Excessive pressure in tank.

name: scan0059-text-0539
text: 8. Punctured float.

name: scan0059-text-0540
text: III. Defective Altitude Control.—When this is in

name: scan0059-text-0541
text: order, opening the cocks fully should reduce the engine

name: scan0059-text-0542
text: speed from 1,400 r.p.m. to about 1,200 r.p.m. at ground

name: scan0059-text-0543
text: level. Needless to say, this test should only be made

name: scan0059-text-0544
text: with the machine chocked and stationary, and the test

name: scan0059-text-0545
text: should be barely long enough for the tachometer needle

name: scan0059-text-0546
text: to record the drop. Such a test will not be made in

name: scan0059-text-0547
text: flight; and if the altitude control should be held open

name: scan0059-text-0548
text: for more than a few seconds in a ground level test, the

name: scan0059-text-0549
text: engine might catch fire.

name: scan0059-text-0550
text: No trouble can arise with the altitude control ex-

name: scan0059-text-0551
text: cept as the result of wear, dirt, careless adjustment of

name: scan0059-text-0552
text: the control linkage, or unwarranted interferences with

name: scan0059-text-0553
text: the parts.

name: scan0059-text-0554
text: As explained on p. 48, a carburettor setting which

name: scan0059-text-0555
text: is correct at ground level will be far too rich at altitude

name: scan0059-text-0556
text: unless special precautions are taken. The vacuum sys-

name: scan0059-text-0557
text: tem is adopted in the H.C. 7 carburettor.

name: scan0059-text-0558
text: The petrol supply from the float to the jet depends

name: scan0059-text-0559
text: on differences of pressure, as explained on page 48. The

name: scan0059-text-0560
text: rate of supply can thus be slowed down by reducing the

name: scan0059-text-0561
text: pressure in the float chamber. This is easily arranged.

name: scan0059-text-0562
text: The cover of the float chamber is provided with an air-

name: scan0059-text-0563
text: tight joint, and air is supplied to the float chamber

name: scan0059-text-0564
text: through a permanent “leak hole” of small diameter,

name: scan0060-text-0566
text: THE USE OF THE VACUUM CONTROL.

name: scan0060-text-0567
text: opening into the atmosphere. In addition, the air space

name: scan0060-text-0568
text: in the float chamber is coupled to the depression area

name: scan0060-text-0569
text: in the mixing chamber by means of a duct known as a

name: scan0060-text-0570
text: “suction hole”; this duct is controlled by a cock and

name: scan0060-text-0571
text: lever. At ground level the suction hole is shut: the

name: scan0060-text-0572
text: float chamber receives air at atmospheric pressure

name: scan0060-text-0573
text: through the leak hole: the maximum contrast exists

name: scan0060-text-0574
text: between the air pressures in the float and mixing cham-

name: scan0060-text-0575
text: bers, respectively: and the full petrol supply is obtained.

name: scan0060-text-0576
text: As the aeroplane climbs, and a reduction in the petrol

name: scan0060-text-0577
text: supply becomes essential, the suction hole is progressively

name: scan0060-text-0578
text: opened by means of the cock. The pressure in the

name: scan0060-text-0579
text: float chamber is proportionately reduced; and the petrol

name: scan0060-text-0580
text: supply is correspondingly cut down. Figs. 48-50 illus-

name: scan0060-text-0581
text: trate the manner in which this system is applied to the

name: scan0060-text-0583
text: The cock should always be kept closed at ground

name: scan0060-text-0584
text: level: otherwise the weak mixture will overheat the

name: scan0060-text-0585
text: engine, and, in addition, there is real danger of fire if

name: scan0060-text-0586
text: the cock is opened wide for more than a few seconds.
